rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: locale?
rows.notes: Falls back to the environment, then to `en-US`. Never a hard-coded table.

rows.name: value?
rows.notes: Controlled. `null` is a value — it means no date is chosen.

rows.name: focusedValue?
rows.notes: The roving anchor, and what decides which page is on screen.

rows.name: today?
rows.notes: Today, injected. A server in UTC and a client in `Pacific/Auckland` are not on the same day, so the machine reads no clock for `data-today` until the first client `ENVIRONMENT.SYNC` — pass this to make the render deterministic.

rows.name: isDateUnavailable?
rows.notes: Consulted in the day view only: it is a predicate over a date.

rows.name: firstDayOfWeek?
rows.notes: ISO numbering, 1 is Monday. Falls back to `Intl.Locale`'s week info.

rows.name: fixedWeeks?
rows.notes: Six rows whatever the month, so the surface stops changing height.

rows.name: views?
rows.notes: The views the `viewTrigger` can open, coarsest last — and it opens **one** of them. The trigger is a disclosure and not a rotation: from the day grid it opens `views[1]`, and from any other view it closes all the way back to `views[0]`. A third entry is therefore never reached by the trigger, which is also what makes `["day", "year"]` the way to put the decade grid one click away. Drilling is a separate gesture and this list does not filter it: clicking a year in the decade grid opens the month grid whether or not `"month"` is here.

rows.name: invalid?
rows.notes: Styling and `aria-invalid` only — a calendar cannot itself be wrong.

rows.name: labelledBy?
rows.notes: Ids naming the grid. Wins over the caption the grid names itself with — a consumer who supplies this owns the whole accessible name.

rows.name: describedBy?
rows.notes: Ids of the text describing this control — a `field` supplies them.

rows.name: autoFocus?
rows.notes: Puts the focus on the focused cell once the grid is mounted.

rows.name: intents?
rows.notes: Where the d-pad arrives from. `null` when the app runs no input system.

rows.name: prevLabel
rows.notes: Names the button that pages backwards, and it is required: see the header.

rows.name: nextLabel
rows.notes: Names the button that pages forwards, and it is required: see the header.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The calendar's visible label. Omitted, no label part is placed.

rows.name: weekdayRow?
rows.notes: The row of day names. It removes itself in the month and year views, where the machine reports no weekdays, so an entry here reaches a row that is not always rendered — the same contract the part itself carries.
